title: Cap. VII: first rock — creating some to destroy; Prosper and Hos. 13:9
pass_a_gloss: One, by which one strikes upon the Divine Goodness; against which those seem to sin, who teach that God by absolute primary will, preceding every consideration of sin, created certain ones that he might destroy them: and from this will of destroying they think there flows whatever is done by God concerning the non-elect. We rather judge with Prosper that it is to be said, There is one cause of being born, another of perishing: That men are born is the Creator's benefit; that they perish is the transgressor's desert. They are indeed created by God, whom he foresaw would never be partakers of eternal life; they are created, whom he decreed to use their free choice, and that by no means propped by special grace; they are created finally, whom he decreed most justly to subject to damnation on account of sins. Meantime this perdition or damnation is to be estimated not as the end of creation, but as the wage of transgression — that that of God in Hosea may always stand, Thy destruction is from thee, Hos. 13:9.
pass_b_english: First rock: striking divine Goodness — those who teach God by absolute primary will, before any regard to sin, created some in order to destroy them, and that from that destroying will flows whatever God does about the non-elect. With Prosper we rather say: one cause of being born, another of perishing — birth is the Creator's benefit; perishing is the transgressor's desert. God does create those he foresaw would never share eternal life; those he decreed to use free choice with no special grace undergirding it; those he decreed most justly to subject to damnation for sins. Yet that perdition or damnation is not creation's end but transgression's wage — so Hosea may always stand: Your destruction is from you (Hos. 13:9).
source_text: Unus, quo impingitur in Bonitatem Divinam; in quam illi peccare videntur, qui docent Deum absoluta primaria voluntate, omnem peccati considerationem antecedente, quosdam creasse ut perderet: atque ex hac perdendi voluntate putant dimanare quicquid circa non-electos a Deo agitur. Nos cum Prospero potius dicendum arbitramur, Aliam esse nascendi, aliam pereundi causam: Ut nascantur homines, Conditoris esse beneficium; ut pereant, praevaricatoris esse meritum. Creantur quidem a Deo, quos praevidit aeternae vitae participes nunquam fore; creantur, quos decrevit suo libero arbitrio, idque speciali gratia minime fulto, uti; creantur denique, quos decrevit propter peccata justissime damnationi subjicere. Perditio interim haec sive damnatio non finis creationis, sed merces transgressionis aestimanda est — ut semper stet illud Dei apud Hoseam, Perditio tua ex te, Hos. xiii. 9.
